content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge treats the absence of an active begetting verb for Joseph and the fact that the cited texts do not state Joseph begat as support for holding the defense.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"with the active begetting verb withheld from Joseph in the record of the generations ([L2] egennēthē in Matthew 1:16)","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that admits both readings is such a verse.","room":"The phrase 'a single verse does not state a link or its contrary': one reading forbids using Matthew 1:16's withheld active verb as support for STANDS, while the other would allow it if the judge also cites other verses.","why":"The judge's holding relies on the non-statement or withheld verb in a verse as a reason to hold for the defense, which K-S2 forbids."}
